To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
odor stimulation evoked an increase in spike activity followed by a decrease of spontaneous oscillations in the primary olfactory pathway of slugs.
the spontaneous oscillatory activity in the primary olfactory nerve of the terrestrial slug L. marginatus was negatively correlated with the odor-evoked spike firing.
the spontaneous oscillation in the primary olfactory pathway of the slug is suppressed by the odor-evoked spikes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional significance of spontaneous oscillations in the primary olfactory systems.
the functional significance of spontaneous oscillations in olfactory processing in terrestrial slugs.
the relationship between odor-induced spike activity and spontaneous oscillations in the primary olfactory center of slugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spontaneous oscillation activity is not a random event but a highly organized activity pattern that is involved in the odor processing of the slug.
the odor-evoked spikes are not inhibited by the large oscillations, and that the large oscillation is not inhibited by the spike activity.
odor-evoked spike firing in the tentacular ganglion is negatively correlated with the amplitude of spontaneous field oscillations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
odor stimulation causes a decrease in the oscillations, which in turn causes an increase in the spike activity.
the spontaneous oscillatory activity in the primary olfactory systems of terrestrial slugs is involved in odor processing.
the oscillatory neural activities in the primary olfactory systems may contribute to the odor discrimination and/or memory consolidation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are significant negative correlations between spontaneous oscillations in the primary olfactory systems of slugs and odor-evoked activity in the olfactory pathway.
the negative relationship between odor-evokedspikeactivityand spontaneousoscillationsintheslug Limaxmarginatusislikely to be a result of the inhibition of the oscillations by the spike activity.
the spontaneous oscillation in the tentacular ganglion may play an inhibitory role on odor-evoked spike firing in the olfactory system of L. marginatus.
